BLOCKER: AC-2/AC-3/AC-4 coverage declares `runtime_capability: False` and only unit/config tests; no runtime evidence for sampling-only prod EXPLAIN, live SLO dashboards/alerts, or per-store quota/degradation.

Per-store enforcement is not wired in declared scope: no DB/object/cache/queue adapter files or concrete call sites are listed, so metrics/quota/degradation cannot be demonstrated at store boundaries.
AC-4 has no per-store quota config/schema or quota integration test; `limits/quota.go` and degrade config alone cannot satisfy "quota enforcement ... per store."
MAJOR: `edp_bench_last_run_unixtime` is unlabeled, so stale/failed benchmark runs cannot be alerted per store/scenario; add bounded freshness metric and dead-man alert.
AC-1 lacks quantitative repeatability/regression criteria (variance/tolerance, confidence, host drift); "repeatable" is not objectively testable.
The design claims promtool/Grafana schema validation, but test/control matrix only runs pytest `validate_edp_slo.py`; add promtool and dashboard schema checks in CI.

Two EXPLAIN capture paths are declared (Go `explain.Capture` and Python `scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py`) with no ownership boundary; a prod-usable Python path bypasses Go sampling/redaction/audit.
Static allowlisted EXPLAIN SQL with no tenant parameters may not exercise RLS/tenant-specific plan shapes; tuning baselines are unrepresentative for tenant-scoped stores.
SLO/dashboard generation only after measured baselines leaves no bootstrap/dead-man alert while baselines or generator are missing/failing.
Operator-only SLO/degradation/quota config changes lack versioning/audit/approval; only runtime degradation events are audited.
MINOR: Baseline artifacts need checksum/provenance and immutability policy; path keyed by ticket ID and git SHA is mutable/audit-weak.
`edp_quota_denials_total{scope,store}` leaves `scope` unbounded/undefined; define a bounded label set.
Alert rules/dashboard lack declared severity, routing/ownership, and runbook URLs for operator response.
`--allow-skip` is correctly non-success, but CI/release evidence must forbid it explicitly or skipped stores can leak into AC-1 proof.
EXPLAIN audit/retention/access-control settings are described but no schema/test validates them.
NIT: Baseline path `engineering/benchmarks/BI-PF-1314/...` couples artifacts to one work item; use stable benchmark/version keys.
`edp_bench_last_run_unixtime` singular naming conflicts with per-store benchmark reality.
`scripts/dev/architect_review.py` appears in affected_files but not review scope; mark tooling-only or remove from item scope.
SUMMARY: Design is strong on read-only EXPLAIN, bounded sampling, rollback, and fail-closed degradation, but not Gate-1 ready.
Top blockers are missing runtime acceptance evidence, absent per-store adapter wiring, and no per-store quota configuration/test.
Observability freshness and generated-rule validation need correction before quotas/degradation can be trusted in production.
Resolve BLOCKER/MAJOR items and attach dispositions under CL-006 before approval.
